To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pigs immunized with E. coli expressing F18ab or with E. coli that express F 18ac fimbriae are protected against colonization with homologous or with heterologous strains.
pigs actively acquire immunity to F18 fimbriated porcine ETEC and ETEE.
actively acquired immunity to ETEC and ETEEC is directed against a common antigenic component of the F18 fimbrial antigen, which is responsible for colonization of the small intestine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an active immunity against E. coli F18 fimbrial variants.
the role of F18 fimbrial antigens for actively acquired immunity in pigs.
the role of fimbria F18 in the development of actively acquired immunity against ETEC and ETEEC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
actively acquired immunity against E. coli strains expressing F18 fimbriate is strain-specific.
the pigs were immunized against colonization by F18 fimbriated enteric E. coli.

the F18 fimbrial antigens are immunogenic and induce an immune response in pigs that is associated with a reduction in colonization of the small intestine with E. coli expressing these fimbriae, but that the F18ab antigen is immunodominant over the F18ac antigen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
F18 fimbriation is not a prerequisite to acquire immunity against colonization with F18 fimbrial strains.
the F18 fimbrial antigen may not be a suitable target for vaccination against ETEC and/or ETEEC infections in pigs.
the production of antibodies against F-18 fimbria is responsible for crosswise protection against F-18ab and F-18ac fimbriated strains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the F18ab or 18ac antigenic variants are not sufficient to provide protection against the heterologous variant.

F18ac is an important virulence factor for the colonization of the small intestine and that the production of F18-specific IgG, IgM and especially IgA antibodies is associated with the prevention of colonization.
F18ab and 18ac are not immunologically distinct.
